R301.note: Clean bounds check (field_index >= MAX_FIELDS) before the array access, returns -1 consistent with existing error convention.

R302.note: Import block declares both a bogus `"metadata"` package and `"google.golang.org/grpc/metadata"` (name collision / nonexistent path) so it won't compile; validateToken() is a stub that authenticates any non-empty string as a fixed "user123", so it doesn't actually enforce identity.

R303.note: Removes the double URL-decode and validates the filename is a single path component that resolves inside the canonical base dir; exceptions are caught by the existing try/catch.

R304.note: Swaps mt_rand(seed,...) for random_bytes(16)/bin2hex; token format changes from a numeric range to a 32-char hex string, an expected side effect of using a real CSPRNG token.

R305.note: RESP length-prefixed encoding correctly neutralizes embedded CRLF/space delimiters and preserves the same recv-based response.

R306.note: Registers the real @fastify/csrf-protection plugin and its csrfProtection preHandler correctly; requiring a token going forward is the intended, disclosed effect of the fix, not incidental breakage.

R307.note: snprintf-based rebuild matches the stated contract exactly: writes "AUDIT user:action" and returns 0 when it fits, rejects (-1) rather than truncating when it doesn't.

R308.note: Correctly swaps the inverted admin/non-admin branches (the actual defect), but also adds Gate::authorize('viewAll'/'viewOwn') calls for abilities that are never registered anywhere in the fix; an unregistered Laravel gate denies by default, which would 403 every caller until those abilities are defined elsewhere -- disclosed in prose but not resolved.

R309.note: Captures bytesSent() into a local before the possible reset(), eliminating the dangling dereference while always returning the original send's byte count.

R310.note: Removes the is_staff queryset-widening exception so all users (including staff) are scoped by owner, matching the documented access policy that IsTicketOwner was meant to enforce.

R311.note: resolve_entities=False plus load_dtd=False closes XXE; correctly notes no_network=True is already the lxml default.

R312.note: Logs the full exception server-side and returns a generic client message; closes the info leak with no other observable change.

R313.note: Imports "bytes" but never uses it anywhere in the file, so Go will fail with "imported and not used: bytes"; otherwise the content-sniffing/allowlist/random-filename/path-containment logic is sound and preserves the stored-name response contract.

R314.note: Canonicalizes both paths and checks the relative path for traversal or rootedness, correctly also catching the Path.Combine-ignores-basePath-on-rooted-input edge case.

R315.note: OdbcCommand uses positional '?' parameters so the AddWithValue name is cosmetic only; binds correctly and preserves the LIKE wildcard semantics.

R316.note: The added validation snippet calls response.sendError() and a bare `return;` inside private String runPing(String host), where `response` is out of scope and the method must return a String -- won't compile as given.

R317.note: Allowlist of category->method exactly matches the one real registered method (email.send), closing the dynamic-dispatch sink without disturbing legitimate calls.

R318.note: Correct, minimal fix (HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode on both fields); the write-up's 'Source' section confusingly shows the already-fixed file rather than the original, but the fix itself is right.

R319.note: expr-eval is a real, purpose-built parser with no runtime/scope access; response shape preserved.

R320.note: `var sql = $"..."` infers sql as plain string (interpolated-string natural type), but FromSqlInterpolated requires FormattableString -- passing a string there does not compile, and the interpolation structure needed for parameterization is already lost. This is exactly the trap the case calls out (renaming the call while still building sql as a string).

R321.note: th:utext -> th:text is the correct, minimal fix; Thymeleaf's built-in escaping is appropriate for this HTML-body context.

R322.note: Named replacements (:startDate/:endDate) correctly parameterize the query; response shape unchanged.

R323.note: StackExchange.Redis HashSet() call is API-correct and closes the CRLF injection, but the fix also replaces the class's public constructor dependency (Socket -> IDatabase), breaking every existing caller; disclosed in the explanation but not a drop-in change.

R324.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) is a real, correct CSPRNG API; output encoding/shape unchanged.

R325.note: The 'vulnerable' and 'fixed' code shown (Express router.post, Mongoose-style Project.findOne(..., callback)) does not match the actual case files at all (router.get, loadProjectExport(projectId) in projectStore.js, no Mongoose model) -- the fix never touches the real vulnerable code.

R326.note: Correctly prefers self.get_object() (applies both queryset scoping and object permissions, avoiding the existence-oracle the case explicitly warns about) and clearly explains why the check_object_permissions alternative is weaker.

R327.note: Captures next before free(), exactly the prescribed fix; preserves traversal order and continues past expired nodes.

R328.note: Correctly adds content-sniffing, allowlist, re-encode, and random server-side filenames; but the JSON response silently changes from {status, path} to {status, filename} (key renamed, full path no longer returned) without calling out the contract change.

R329.note: Passes requestedCapacity instead of the stale MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY constant, exactly the prescribed one-line fix.

R330.note: `Message message = new MimeMessage(session)` then calls `message.setRecipients(RecipientType.TO, recipientEmail)` with a String -- that overload only exists on MimeMessage, not the declared Message type, so it won't compile.

R331.note: Adds secure=True (the actual finding) plus samesite='Lax'; no other observable change.

R332.note: The primary fix calls stream.ReadAtLeastAsync(header, 0, header.Length, throwOnEndOfStream: true), which doesn't match the real signature (Memory<byte>, int minimumBytes, bool, CancellationToken) -- passing header.Length positionally where a bool is expected won't compile; the given pre-.NET-7 fallback (checking bytesRead < header.Length) is correct and usable on its own.

R333.note: Moves from denylist to allowlist but still trusts the client-supplied extension and MIME type with no content-sniffing, so a mislabeled or double-extension file (e.g. shell.php.jpg) with a spoofed image/jpeg header still passes -- the exact residual gap the finding named.

R334.note: Replaces the subprocess/tar invocation with Python's tarfile module entirely, removing the injection surface; filenames starting with '-' are naturally treated as literal paths, satisfying the stated contract.

R335.note: mysqli prepared statement with bind_param preserves the original return semantics (null on failure, first row via fetch_assoc).

R336.note: Removes the stray [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken], restoring the app-wide antiforgery filter exactly as the code comment indicates was intended; matches the case's own description precisely.

R337.note: Same correct capture-next-before-free fix as R327.

R338.note: escapeHTML applied to both untrusted fields only; CGI.pm's method-name import mechanism supports `use CGI qw(escapeHTML)`, no other behavior change.

R339.note: Replaces the injectable assert(string) with a direct boolean check/throw, matching the documented intent ("Confirms the requesting account is entitled to a premium-only report") rather than relying on assert(), which is a no-op in typical production php.ini settings anyway.

R340.note: On Windows, subprocess.Popen([bat_path, ...], shell=False) cannot launch a .bat file directly (CreateProcess needs shell=True or an explicit ['cmd','/c', ...] wrapper) -- the fix closes the shell-injection vector but silently breaks the actual export_report.bat invocation on the target host without saying so.
